updates.html: BUILDER HANDOFF · STORAGE REPAIR VERIFIED · NAVIGATION CONTINUES · 9 NOV 2026

Paper states 09–16 extend the existing R4 candidate. Snapshot safety is now implemented in Macro PR #10901 · head 2c04fc37d239f4bf27b6efaed98b229256ea337e · dependent open Draft. It preserves the PR #9580 parent at 5e496c24c962e85a4f7f514dd43dc61443b95cab. These are historical source fixtures, not personal saved records. Parent return, route-horizon continuity and the frozen-case layout remain the next implementation phase.

Continue in templates/crypto_intelligence_r4.js and the existing drawer, hash-route and local-storage owners. PR #10901 implements the storage repair; template and served JS are identical. Its two saved pages change only asset-version references. CSS, HTML template, builder and source data remain unchanged. Source and proof: research/design_candidates/crypto_snapshot_safety_20261109/.

30-day fixture: revision r4-display:2026-10-17:30:continuation; BTC; cutoff 17 Oct 2026; expiry 16 Nov 2026; daily close above $86,595, then stronger spot demand. Its 60 prior closes run 18 Aug–16 Oct; low $64,681. The older 7-day failure fixture uses $81,566 and expires 24 Oct. Do not substitute the 7-day range into the 30-day case. The existing test anchor is 18 Oct 2026 at 12:00 UTC; new synthetic preservation tests also retain an explicitly older save time and evidence digest.

Implemented in PR #10901: the existing mmx.crypto.r4.scenarios.v1 reader separates a ready full collection from unavailable storage. saved-item:<revision> and memory-saved:<revision> require one usable exact match, supported numeric horizon, real cutoff/expiry dates and original bilingual case fields. Duplicate, malformed, missing or unreadable requested versions cannot borrow current scenario data.

The memory-saved fallback to horizon() and data.as_of is removed. An unreadable collection uses state 16; an unusable requested version remains unavailable without current context. A missing issue_evidence digest alone does not invalidate an otherwise usable legacy case. The richer state 11 destination controls remain part of the next navigation/layout phase.

Implemented in PR #10901: Save and Remove are explicit intents captured from the displayed action. Save when already present makes no write and preserves saved_at and issue_evidence. Remove deletes every exact revision match across the full collection and preserves unrelated parsed entries and their order. Already-absent Remove makes no write and never appends. Only an actual new Save applies the existing 50-snapshot retention policy; opaque entries survive.

Read/parse/shape failures prevent mutation. One write is followed by exact serialized readback before success is announced. Throws, dropped writes, failed or mismatched readback are unconfirmed: no automatic retry or redirect. Completion cannot replace a newer focused control or steal focus after a callback opens another panel. Web Storage read/write/readback does not provide atomic cross-tab compare-and-swap.

State 11 remains an unavailable requested version with no borrowed asset, horizon, cutoff or condition. Its “Open saved snapshots” and deliberate “Open current outlook” controls are the next layout/navigation work. Implemented state 16 copy is “Saved snapshots unavailable” / “Saved snapshots couldn’t be read.” “Try reading again” invokes the existing reader; no background retry owner is added.

Use “No changes were made” only for a failure before writing. A confirmed removal may be followed by a failed list read, so the general unavailable-list message must remain neutral. Already-absent removal: “This snapshot is no longer saved on this device.” Unconfirmed write: “The change couldn’t be confirmed. Check Saved snapshots before trying again.” Do not call an unreadable collection empty. Legacy state 14 keeps its original case and missing-digest explanation.

Verified in PR #10901: 40 real-browser cases, 41 fresh contexts / 47 pages, Chrome 157.0.8103.39, zero page errors; the existing 32 view/theme/locale/width permutations are retained. All 39 existing contract cases have passing coverage: 36 passed with the browser suite, then three missing-import cases passed after exact-parent dependency hydration. Initial 76 passed / 3 failed and later 3 passed receipts are preserved; no single-run 79-pass claim. Eight final native dialog crops were inspected.

Still required next: 30-day saved item from a 7-day view → review → parent → Close back to 7 days; detached saved-item parent and truly detached review; native Back/Forward; same-revision disclosure, scroll, semantic focus and locale continuity; missing record during return; visible-opener fallback. At 320px and 390px, verify target sizes and reduced motion. Locale changes must create no history entry or storage write. Dialog crops alone do not prove desktop full-viewport toast placement.

Paper states 09–16 remain the full applied design amendment. The storage and confirmation portion is implemented and locally verified at PR #10901 head 2c04fc37d239f4bf27b6efaed98b229256ea337e; the original-condition-first hierarchy and navigation/reading-state requirements remain active work. No merge, deployment, hosted/independent visual acceptance or production replacement is claimed.

Preserve original R4 source drawer GB-0, scenario page BB-0, alert integration gate HE-0 and public-route cutover gate QQ-0. H5/model authority remains held. Keep the existing owners and verify each actual journey. Historical fixtures and synthetic local storage do not establish current freshness, personal activity, forecast skill, model allocation or alert delivery.

Saved cases: preserve identity, return precisely.
Paper states 09–16 extend the existing R4 candidate. Macro PR #9580 · head 5e496c24c962e85a4f7f514dd43dc61443b95cab · open draft. These are source-backed historical fixtures, not personal saved records or current market advice. Runtime changes and browser proof remain pending.
01 · Source & fixtures
Change the existing templates/crypto_intelligence_r4.js and companion CSS; keep scripts/build_crypto_intelligence_r4.py, the hash route owner and local storage owner. Candidate source is PR #9580 at 5e496c24c962e85a4f7f514dd43dc61443b95cab, not merged production.

30-day fixture: revision r4-display:2026-10-17:30:continuation; BTC; cutoff 17 Oct 2026; expiry 16 Nov 2026; daily close above $86,595, then stronger spot demand. Its 60 prior closes run 18 Aug–16 Oct; low $64,681. The older 7-day failure fixture uses $81,566 and expires 24 Oct. Do not substitute the 7-day range into the 30-day case. Fixture saved_at is the existing test anchor, 18 Oct 2026 at 12:00 UTC; it is not evidence of a personal save.
02 · Resolve the saved record
Use the existing mmx.crypto.r4.scenarios.v1 owner. Before rendering or acting on saved-item:<revision> or memory-saved:<revision>, resolve one usable record with that exact revision. Validate original authority, supported saved horizon, cutoff and original case fields; do not default an invalid horizon to 7. Duplicate, malformed, missing or unreadable records must not acquire current scenario data.

The current memory-saved branch falls back to horizon() and data.as_of when lookup fails. Replace that branch with state 11 for an unavailable requested version or state 16 for an unreadable collection, with explicit recovery. Preserve the distinction between an empty list, an unavailable storage read and a missing requested version. A missing issue_evidence digest alone does not invalidate an otherwise usable legacy case.
03 · Return is a parent action
Managed review with a verified immediate saved-item parent for the same revision → “← Saved case” → history.back() once. Verify the current saved record again before the action. A review opened from a detached saved-item can still have a valid parent; detachedOrigin alone is not a reason to discard it.

Valid saved record, but no verified immediate parent → “Open saved case” → replace the current entry with that exact saved-item through the existing update owner. Missing or unusable record → “Open saved snapshots”, never another version. Close remains the existing whole-drawer journey exit; do not call close() to implement parent return. Do not add a parallel router, history stack or saved-case store.
04 · Keep horizons separate
Opening a saved list item must pass its validated s.horizon_days to the existing open() function. A 30-day saved case opened from the 7-day view stays 30-day through review and parent return. The ancestor list and underlying current view remain 7-day when the drawer journey closes. Repair a legacy parent URL in the same history entry if required; do not insert a second parent or overwrite the outer origin.

Map original 7-day item H4-0 to state 14 / 3BM-0. The added 30-day list item maps to state 09 / 3BC-0. Review is state 10 / 3BE-0; detached review is state 15 / 3BO-0; unavailable is state 11 / 3BG-0. State 12 / 3BI-0 is the same saved-item with its evidence disclosure open, not another route.
05 · Original condition first
For frozen cases, show the saved title, asset, horizon, cutoff, original status and condition before the details. Keep the saved sequence, invalidation, counter-evidence, expiry and level basis in the existing native details pattern under “Original case details”. Keep a single “Original evidence” disclosure. Read only the captured issue_evidence fields; never reconstruct missing legacy evidence from current data.families.

State 12 shows six saved families. Their dates come from snapshot_as_of, not verified observation dates. Bitcoin cutoff is 17 Oct; broader market is 15 Oct; Participation also retains 15 Oct. “Stale at capture” and “Snapshot only” describe the original quality. Expiry is distinct from cutoff and save time. Conditional research is not a probability or a validated performance result.
06 · Focus, scroll & motion
Use the existing dialog as the scroll owner; its header is sticky. Do not create a second nested scrolling body. Fit 390px and 320px widths; parent and Close targets are at least 44px, primary action 48px, disclosures at least 44px. Native details preserve keyboard semantics. The current Paper frames demonstrate content fit, not a browser viewport or scroll test.

renderDrawer() replaces its children. Preserve a serializable semantic locator for the exact saved revision and Historical review action, then focus the recreated control on parent return. Do not retain a detached inner DOM node or overwrite the outer lastTrigger. Restore disclosure state and scroll only for the same valid revision. Locale changes retain these states; missing controls fall back to the saved-case heading. Outer Close restores only a connected, visible opener in the active view, otherwise that view’s heading. Preserve current reduced-motion behavior; no attention animation or fabricated live pulse.
07 · Explicit save & remove
Replace toggle-by-fresh-state semantics inside the existing save owner with an explicit save or remove intent captured from the action. Save when absent follows existing eligibility; save when already present is a no-op and preserves saved_at and issue_evidence. Remove deletes all exact revision matches and preserves unrelated entries. Remove when already absent is a no-write completion, never an append or a fresh evidence capture.

Read storage into a ready/unavailable result before any mutation. Keep the full valid collection separate from display filtering; do not use filtered/sliced rendered items as the preservation source. Unreadable JSON, access failure or unusable collection means no write. Preserve existing retention policy only for an actual save; do not use this repair for cleanup or migration. Verify the intended postcondition before claiming success; an uncertain write is not replayed automatically.
08 · Honest recovery & copy
State 11 is an unavailable requested version; show no borrowed asset, horizon, cutoff or condition. “Open saved snapshots” is the primary destination; “Open current outlook” is a deliberate separate action. State 16 is a failed collection read: “Saved snapshots unavailable” / “Saved snapshots couldn’t be read. No changes were made.” Its “Try reading again” button invokes the same existing reader once, with no new background retry owner.

Already-absent removal: “This snapshot is no longer saved on this device.” Unconfirmed write: “Couldn’t confirm removal. Check saved snapshots before trying again.” Use the equivalent save wording for Save. Do not say “Nothing saved yet” on a failed read. Legacy state 14 keeps its original case and says “Source details not saved”; it does not imply the record itself is missing.
09 · Required browser proof
Extend tests/test_crypto_intelligence_r4_browser.py. Existing tests cover the route/viewport matrix, a 30-day deep link, saved original evidence, missing current scenario, legacy digest and short mobile evidence scroll. They do not prove a named saved-case parent return or the missing memory-saved guard.

Prove 30-day saved item opened from a 7-day view → review → parent → Close back to 7 days; detached saved-item with valid parent; truly detached review; missing, malformed and duplicate revisions; storage access/parse/shape failures with zero writes; stale Remove with no re-addition; stale Save preserving the first saved payload; removal of all duplicate matches preserving unrelated entries; failed write/readback without false success or automatic replay. At 320px and 390px, verify keyboard focus, scroll, disclosure/locale continuity and reduced motion. A locale change must create no history entry or storage write.
10 · Delivery & acceptance
Paper states 09–16 and this Build sheet are an applied design amendment. The source diagnosis is pinned to the PR head above; no new runtime implementation, browser execution, automated test pass, merge or deployment is claimed here. Preserve original R4 source drawer GB-0, scenario page BB-0, alert integration gate HE-0 and public-route cutover gate QQ-0. The newer relative-comparison page remains separate and unchanged.

When implementing, keep the existing local snapshot, drawer, URL, language and toast owners. Read back the owned diff, run affected checks and prove the actual journey before accepting it. A source fixture demonstrates a historical design state only; it does not establish current freshness, personal activity, forecast performance, model allocation or alert delivery.
